title: Preparing to Inherit the Promised Land

date.label: Undated biblical wilderness narrative and legislation
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The received Numbers narrative contains the preparing to inherit the promised land material across Numbers 32–36.
claims.evidence: Numbers 32–36; biblical-text description, not independent evidence for an event date.

claims.claim: The exact archaeological or external historical setting of this entire passage has not been independently established.
claims.evidence: Phase 1 Dossier Ten and Phase 2 N10-04: MacDonald (East of the Jordan, ch. 5, pp. 66–67, read directly; confirmed by QA Phase 4 §5.10) finds the Numbers, Deuteronomy and Judges itineraries irreconcilable, with many Num 33 stations unidentified or disputed; QA Phase 4 §5.10 records no site identification and no verified ANE equivalent for the Num 35 refuge system.

claims.claim: Comparisons with related biblical laws and retellings need to preserve differences in wording, chronology, or institutional setting.
claims.evidence: Internal textual comparisons documented in CONNECTION-AUDIT.md; interpretation of literary relationship, not an archaeological observation.

connections.note: Refuge-law parallel; the laws differ concretely: cities — altar asylum in Exodus 21:12–14, three cities plus three more conditionally in Deuteronomy 19:2, 8–9, six in Numbers 35:6 (three of them set apart in Deuteronomy 4:41–43); procedure — the congregation judges in Numbers 35:24–25, the elders of the slayer’s own city fetch him in Deuteronomy 19:12, the elders of the refuge city hear his cause in Joshua 20:4; rationale — only Numbers states the land-pollution theology (35:33–34); terminus — release at the high priest’s death in Numbers 35:25, 28 (and Joshua 20:6), with no such terminus in Deuteronomy 19 or Exodus 21.
Later implementation account of cities of refuge.

Jephthah’s message to the Ammonite king retells the Transjordan passage — Israel’s refusal of passage, the defeat of Sihon, and possession from Arnon to Jabbok (11:22). MacDonald treats Judges 11 as an itinerary parallel that cannot be harmonized with Numbers 33.

Later implementation of the Numbers 34 allotment: the tribal inheritances divided by lot at Shiloh (19:51), using overlapping geographic language with different detail — compare, do not force onto one map.

Altar-asylum parallel: the unintentional killer flees to an appointed place (21:13), but the presumptuous killer is taken from the altar (21:14) — no cities, no congregation trial, no high-priest terminus.
Original Zelophehad ruling — the daughters’ plea generalized into an inheritance statute (27:11) — which Numbers 36 then qualifies with the endogamy restriction.
